data.title: The Bowling Ball
data.rumour: There's a candlepin ball that rattles like a maraca, and the man who owns it won't let anybody look inside.
about: A small mystery in a bowling ball. Arlo Lund sells his late father's candlepin ball, which rattles (§{ballArlo}). His father was league treasurer in 1979, the year the league's money went missing, and people still talk.

The next morning you can drill out the plug. Inside is a key to locker 9 at Pinwheel Lanes. With Bev and Arlo at the lanes (§{ballLocker}), and something to cut or pry the old lock, you find $1,240 in 1979 bills and a note: Gunnar Lund hid the new-lanes fund from the owner, who was about to skip town with it. Give it all to the league (The Gunnar Lund Trophy) or take a finder's fee and split it with Arlo (Finder's Fee). Selling the ball unopened is Still Rattling.

lundBall.name: Gunnar Lund's candlepin ball
tells: Purple, small enough to hold in one hand, like every candlepin ball. Something inside it rattles.
A plug of a slightly different purple, sanded flush, on one side.

overheard.line: Chuckling: "There's a ball on lane four that rattles like a maraca. Bev won't let it on the lanes. Says it's haunted. Says it's worse than haunted, it's uneven."

ballArlo.title: Arlo Lund sells his father's ball

text: Arlo Lund. This was my father's ball. Gunnar Lund. He bowled a hundred and forty with it in 1979 and never let anybody else touch it.
It rattles. Always has. Bev Santos says a rattling ball is bad luck on her lanes. Bev says a lot of things. I could use ten dollars more than I could use a ball.

then.text: Dad was league treasurer, you know. The year the money went. People said things. People still say things.

steps.narrate: Pinwheel Lanes at lunchtime. A league of retirees on lanes one to four. Behind the snack bar, a wall of green lockers nobody has opened since the carpet was new.

steps.text: Locker 9. That's from before me. That's from before the carpet. Arlo, did you know about this?
Dad never said a word. Not one. For forty years people said he took the money.

steps.note: Eli Barrow, if The Barrow Boy is in the run and he hasn't been found out.

then.text: The key's too far gone. I've got bolt cutters. I've got everything. Don't ask why I've got bolt cutters.
The key won't turn. Forty years of snack-bar steam. Tell me you brought something.

narrate.then: You did. The {it.name|lower} does the rest.
narrate.else: You did. It does the rest.

else.text: The key won't turn. Forty years of snack-bar steam. Arlo, the fire axe.
We are not using the fire axe, Bev.

else.narrate: Twenty minutes, a butter knife and most of a can of WD-40 later, the key gives up before the lock does. Bev fetches the hammer from the pinsetter room.

steps.narrate: The locker opens with a noise like a bad knee. Inside: a canvas bank bag, and in it twelve hundred and forty dollars in 1979 bills, rubber-banded, and a letter.

steps.text: "Harold Voss is going to skip town with the new-lanes fund. I've hidden it till the audit. If you're reading this, I didn't get to tell anybody. G.L." Harold Voss owned this place. He left in 1980. With a waitress.
The new-lanes fund. My mother put five dollars a week into that.

choose.label: Give it all to the league

then.text: New pinsetters. Real ones. And the trophy gets a new name. The Gunnar Lund Trophy. Arlo, you're presenting it. In a tie.
He'd hate that. He'd love that.

choose.label: Take a finder's fee and split the rest with Arlo

then.why: A finder's fee from the 1979 league fund

then.text: Fair. You found it. I mean, Dad found it. Then he hid it. Then you found it.
The league will hear about this. The league hears about everything.

mornings.note: The morning after you buy it: open it up?

choose.label: Drill out the plug in the rattling ball

clues.text: Drilled open. It was hollow, and it held a key.

then.narrate: Under the plug, the core is hollow. Out drops a small brass key stamped 9, wrapped in a note in pencil: "LOCKER 9. FOR THE LEAGUE. G.L. 1979."

then.toast: Calendar: locker 9 at Pinwheel Lanes, {placed:ball-locker} at noon

epilogue.line: The Tuesday league bowls for the Gunnar Lund Trophy. Arlo presents it, in a tie, every year.
Pinwheel Lanes still has the old pinsetters. Arlo Lund bought a boat with his half. The league talks about it.
Somewhere a candlepin ball still rattles. Nobody in Hollow Neck ever found out why the new lanes never got built.
